question: A wire carrying a current $I$ along the positive $x$-axis has length $L$. It is kept in a magnetic field $\vec{B} = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k})$ T. The magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the wire is :
solution:
$$\vec{F} = I\vec{L} \times \vec{B} = IL\,\hat{i} \times (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}) = IL(3\hat{k} + 4\hat{j})$$

(using $\hat{i}\times\hat{i} = 0$, $\hat{i}\times\hat{j} = \hat{k}$, $\hat{i}\times\hat{k} = -\hat{j}$).

$$|\vec{F}| = IL\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\,IL$$

(The component of $\vec{B}$ along the wire, $2\hat{i}$, exerts no force.)
